hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated acidified manganate(VII) does to an alkene, it completely breaks the C=C double bond.
Look at but-1-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$, and notice the left side of the double bond has two carbons attached to one ethyl group.
Remember the cleavage rule, a $\text{=CH}_2$ end always becomes $\text{CO}_2$, while a $\text{=CHR}$ group becomes a carboxylic acid, so work out which alkene can give a 3-carbon acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidative cleavage**

Hot, concentrated $\text{MnO}_4^-$ / $\text{H}^+$ is a very strong oxidiser. It breaks the C=C bond completely and oxidises each carbon separately.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{=CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2, \quad \text{=CHR} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}, \quad \text{=CR}_2 \rightarrow \text{RCOR}$$

**Apply the rule to but-1-ene**

Draw but-1-ene as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$. Split it at the double bond.

Left fragment is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=}$, which is of type =CHR, so it is oxidised to a carboxylic acid:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Identify the acid and conclude**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ has 3 carbons, it is propanoic acid. The other $\text{=CH}_2$ end gives $\text{CO}_2$.

So but-1-ene is the alkene that gives propanoic acid as one product.

options.A: But-1-ene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$. Cleavage gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (propanoic acid) from the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=}$ part plus $\text{CO}_2$ from the $\text{=CH}_2$ part. This matches the question exactly.
options.B: But-2-ene is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$. Both sides are =CHCH3, so each gives ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. You get two molecules of a 2-carbon acid, not a 3-carbon propanoic acid.
options.C: 2-methylpropene is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CH}_2$. The $\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)}_2$ side gives the ketone propanone, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=O}$, and the $\text{=CH}_2$ side gives $\text{CO}_2$. No carboxylic acid is formed at all.
options.D: 2-methylbut-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The $\text{=CH}_2$ gives $\text{CO}_2$ and the disubstituted carbon gives the ketone butanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. This is a common trap of confusing a ketone product with a carboxylic acid.
